text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:

- Bilateral negotiations between Switzerland and the European Union on road and rail traffic through Switzerland remained subject to further talks after the latest round on Tuesday in Bussels. Swiss transport minister Moritz Leuenberger said the two sides agreed "conceptually" but must still agree on truck taxation and quotas.
- Foreign minister Flavio Cotti plans to visit several Latin American countries next week.

- Swiss pharma giant Roche reported a 1996 net profit of 3.89 billion Swiss francs, up 16 percent compared to the previous year. Roche plans to introduce several new drugs in order to get sales back on track. Sales climbed only by three percent in the 1997 first quarter compared to the corresponding period last year.

- Swiss cement maker Holderbank said it will shut down its production plant in Rekingen in March 1998, part of cutbacks in mainly European capacity that resulted in an after-tax charge on 1996 accounts of 450 million Swiss francs.
- Swiss machine and transport vehicle manufacturer Bucher reported a 37 percent boost in 1996 net profit to 49.3 million Swiss francs.
- Swiss insurer Helvetia Patria registered a 1996 net profit of 65.2 million Swiss francs, up 35 percent compared to the previous year.
- Swiss restaurant chain Moevenpick reported a 47.4 percent increase in 1996 net profit to 22.4 million Swiss francs.
